item.title: [Due in 1 day] Canada time-zone change on 1 November: Outlook users in BC, Alberta and Manitoba must switch time zone and recheck meetings; an Exchange Online remediation cmdlet is due 28 October
item.description:
Not a security change, but a time-zone shift moves timestamps that sign-in, audit and detection queries correlate across; Teams Rooms devices one hour behind Windows also misreport meeting times.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-11-01 · Before 1 November make sure Windows devices in the affected regions have the October 2026 updates, update Edge and WebView2 on Teams Rooms on Windows, and plan to run the Exchange Online remediation cmdlet for non-recurring meetings once Microsoft releases it (target 28 October).

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 1 day] Outlook on the web and new Outlook will block .msix and .msixbundle attachments by default from early November, in every OWA mailbox policy
item.description:
MSIX packages are an established malware delivery format, so this closes an attachment path by default. The cost falls on teams that distribute line-of-business app packages by mail, which will fail without an error anyone anticipated, and the change reaches custom policies too, not only the default one.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-11-01 · Search mail flow for .msix and .msixbundle attachments over the last 90 days; if a business process depends on them, move it off email rather than adding the types to AllowedFileTypes, and record the decision before early November.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 6 days] Cross-tenant calendar sharing on Cross-Tenant Access Policy slips again, to 6 November; EWS-based Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing keep breaking as EWS is disabled
item.description:
Partners lose sight of free/busy and shared calendars as EWS reaches the tenant; the usual workaround — re-enabling EWS — keeps a legacy, high-privilege API surface open for another five months.

Exchange Online · deadline 2026-11-06 · Run Get-OrganizationRelationship and Get-SharingPolicy as the post shows; migrate Free/Busy and MailTips now and Calendar Sharing after 6 November, and if you set EWSEnabled to True, record it as a time-boxed exception ending 1 April 2027.

item.title: [New] Outlook's Join button stops appearing for meetings whose join URL is HTTP-only, from the week of 30 November 2026
item.description:
An HTTP-only meeting link is a cleartext redirect target; dropping the button removes one click path to it, and an integration still emitting HTTP links is worth finding.

Exchange Online · Ask owners of third-party meeting providers, add-ins and custom integrations to confirm they emit HTTPS join URLs, and validate new invitations before 30 November 2026.

item.title: [Message Center] MC1528007 Join button will require HTTPS meeting links
item.description:
Starting late November 2026, Outlook's Join button will only appear for meetings with HTTPS join URLs. Meetings with HTTP-only URLs will not show the button. Organizations should ensure their meeting providers and integrations generate HTTPS links to avoid impact. No action is needed if HTTPS URLs are already used.

item.title: [New] Exchange Online Change Optics report is GA: it lists onmicrosoft.com external traffic and Direct Send traffic before enforcement
item.description:
Direct Send is a spoofing path that Reject Direct Send closes; the report is the inventory of legitimate senders you need before you switch it on.

Exchange Online · Open the DRS scenario in the Change Optics report, list the legitimate Direct Send senders, move them to a connector or authenticated submission, then enable Reject Direct Send.

item.description:
